comment: Differences between the port and Thaumic Tinkerer 1.7.10 that a deviation text documents. Each entry allows exactly 'occurrences' (default 1) differences with the same subject, field, original value and port value: it is consumed by the difference it matches, a second identical difference is a failure, and an entry that matches less often than it allows is a failure too. 'deviation' is the file below docs/deviations and 'quote' a sentence of it; 'mentions' are names that the passage around the sentence (its paragraph or bullet, the two before it and the heading) has to contain, at least one of them naming the entry's key (KnownDifferencesTest checks all of it). Written by hand; the values are what ParityComparator prints.

differences.reason: BlockAspectAnalyzer.shouldRegister() returned LoadedMods.computerCraftLoaded; the port registers the Aspectalyzer, its research and its recipe always, because without a computer mod the block would otherwise be unobtainable. The position, aspects, parents and pages of the entry are still compared with the original and match.
differences.quote: Without a computer mod the block would be unobtainable, so it is registered always

differences.original: registered by the original only when [LoadedMods.computerCraftLoaded]
differences.reason: The arcane recipe of the Aspectalyzer belongs to the same always-registered block (see the research entry). Its research key, aspects, pattern shape and ingredients are still compared with the original and match.
differences.quote: Without a computer mod the block would be unobtainable, so it is registered always

differences.reason: BlockGolemConnector.shouldRegister() returned LoadedMods.computerCraftLoaded; the port registers the block with its research, recipe and the Binder's golem binding always. The fields of the entry are still compared with the original and match.
differences.quote: The port registers it always, with its research, recipe and the Binder's golem binding

differences.original: registered by the original only when [LoadedMods.computerCraftLoaded]
differences.reason: The arcane recipe of the Golem Connector belongs to the same always-registered block. Its fields are still compared with the original and match.
differences.quote: The port registers it always, with its research, recipe and the Binder's golem binding

differences.reason: 1.7.10 ResearchHelper.initResearch registered the documentation root of the computer peripherals only with ComputerCraft. The Aspectalyzer and the Golem Connector are always registered in the port and are its children in the book, so the root exists too (auto-unlocked, round, at -1,0 like the original).
differences.quote: The entry still exists, because the Aspectalyzer and the Golem Connector are its children in the book

differences.original: never registered (its owner's shouldRegister() is false)
differences.reason: BlockRPlacer.shouldRegister() returned false in the pinned fork, so its research and recipe were dead code there; the port ports the block and registers them. The fields of the entry are still compared with the dead definition and match.
differences.quote: BlockRPlacer.shouldRegister() returned `false` in the pinned fork

differences.reason: 1.7.10 put the Remote Placer research at (-6, 3), the cell of the Magnets research; that only worked because the fork never registered the block (shouldRegister() was false). Registered together with Magnets the second entry would be dropped by Thaumcraft ('overlaps with existing research'), so the lead moved it to (-8, 3), below its parent the Animation Tablet. Row, aspects, complexity, parents and pages are unchanged and compared.
differences.quote: It is at (-8, 3) now, below its parent the Animation Tablet.

differences.original: never registered (its owner's shouldRegister() is false)
differences.reason: The arcane recipe of the Remote Placer was dead code in the fork (the block was never registered); the port registers it with the block. Its fields are still compared with the dead definition and match.
differences.quote:
so it is registered, with its research
  `REMOTE_PLACER` and recipe

differences.port: merged into thaumictinkerer:dark_quartz_0 with the other recipe of the same result
differences.reason: 1.7.10 registered the dark quartz recipe twice under the key DARK_QUARTZ0, once with coal and once with charcoal; the port has one data recipe (dark_quartz_0.json) whose centre ingredient accepts both. The comparison matches the second original recipe with that recipe too: its pattern, result and ingredients are compared like any other, and the merged recipe has to accept exactly the union of the two centre ingredients (coal and charcoal), nothing more.
differences.quote:
The two quartz recipes with coal (`Items.coal` damage 0) and charcoal (damage 1) are one recipe with a two-item
  ingredient.

differences.port: merged into thaumictinkerer:dark_quartz_5 with the other recipe of the same result
differences.reason: 1.7.10 registered the dark quartz stairs recipe twice (a left and a right staircase, both mirror images); shaped recipes of 1.21.1 are mirrored by default, so the port has one recipe (dark_quartz_5.json) for both. The comparison matches the second original recipe with it too, as the mirror image of its pattern, and the slots have to accept exactly the union of the two.
differences.quote:
The stairs recipe came twice (a left and a right staircase). Shaped recipes of 1.21.1 are mirrored by default: one
  recipe

differences.original: the 23 item-owned Kami entries never required a block-owned research of the add-on (TTRegistry.postInit registers the research of the items before that of the blocks) and only the item-owned research registered before each (HashMap order); [WARP_GATE] (block-owned) required the block-owned research registered before it; Thaumcraft's five tabs and ResearchHelper's research were required by all
differences.port: every Kami entry requires the union: all other non-Kami research of the six tabs, the block-owned research of the add-on included
differences.reason: KamiResearchItem.setPages of 1.7.10 collected the research registered at that moment; the research of every item is registered before that of any block, and the iteration order of the registry's HashMap decided the rest, so the set was never complete for the item-owned entries and not reproducible. The port collects the requirements after all other research is registered: the union, a superset of every set 1.7.10 could produce. The comparison checks the port's list against exactly the union (six tabs, minus lost, virtual, Kami, MINILITH*, *KAMI), in order after the explicit hidden parents.
differences.quote:
The port collects the requirements in `KamiResearchItem.registerResearch()`, after all other research is registered, so every Kami entry
requires all of them
